title: Stalk of the pullback of a module, and germs of pulled-back sections
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, with $f^\sharp_x:\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ the induced map of local rings, and let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_Y$-module with pullback $f^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For an open $V\subseteq Y$ and $s\in\mathcal G(V)$ write $f^*s\in(f^*\mathcal G)(f^{-1}V)$ for the image of $s$ under the unit $\mathcal G\to f_*f^*\mathcal G$ of the adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$. Then for every $x\in X$, with $y=f(x)$, there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules
$$(f^*\mathcal G)_x\;\cong\;\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{X,x}$$
(the tensor product formed with $f^\sharp_x$), natural in $\mathcal G$, under which the germ $(f^*s)_x$ of $f^*s$ (for $V\ni y$, $s\in\mathcal G(V)$) corresponds to $s_y\otimes1$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 6.26.4 (Tag 0098, label lemma-stalk-pullback-modules), proof via Lemma Tag 008B (lemma-stalk-tensor-sheaf-modules) and the stalks of $f^{-1}$; the description of the germs of $f^*s$ is part of the construction of the isomorphism (the stalk of the unit $\mathcal G\to f_*f^*\mathcal G$ at $y$ composed with $(f_*f^*\mathcal G)_y\to(f^*\mathcal G)_x$)

proof.text: Obtain β and its germ formula from lem-pc-inverse-image-stalk-scalar-transport. Apply SheafOfModules.stalkChangeOfRingsIso to tensorPullbackRingMap f and inverseImageModule f.base Y.sheaf G, obtaining τ and its pure-tensor germ formula. Form δ_G=β_G followed by τ_G, an isomorphism from extension of scalars of G_y to the stalk of tensorPullback f G.

Evaluate δ_G on 1 tensor germ(s). The β formula followed by the τ formula, with coefficient section 1, yields the germ of the sheafification unit applied to 1 tensor η_G(s). The chosen canonical adjunction unit formula in exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction identifies this with the germ of the pulled-back section. This is hδ in Lean.

Prove naturality of δ using ModuleCat.ExtendScalars.hom_ext, which reduces it to 1 tensor m. Represent m by a germ(s). The stalk-map germ formula sends m to germ(a(s)), and extendScalars.map_tmul computes its tensor image. On both sides use hδ. Naturality of the chosen adjunction unit says tensorPullback(a)(unit_G(s))=unit_H(a(s)); the stalk-map germ formula turns this section equality into the required stalk equality. NatIso.ofComponents now gives a natural isomorphism d.

Take e=d inverse. Apply δ_G inverse to hδ; the inverse-after-forward identity gives e_G(germ(pulled-back s))=1 tensor germ(s), exactly the required formula. No naturality assumption on β or τ is needed.
